original_query: Is Penetration of the book, access levels of which range from public domain to short term loan or rentals, higher in Public or Academic libraries?

summaries.found_via_query: Comparison of book penetration rates in public vs. academic libraries based on access levels (public domain, short term loan, rentals)
summaries.summary: A diagram titled 'eBook Access Levels' illustrates a spectrum from 'Public Domain' to 'Short Term Loan or Rentals', with various access levels marked along a gradient. These include Open Access, Locally Hosted (DRM), Perpetual Access (No Fees), Perpetual Access (Fees paid up front), Perpetual Access (Ongoing Fees), Limits on Circulation, and Subscription. The diagram visually represents increasing restrictions and costs as one moves from left to right.
key_facts: The diagram shows a continuum of eBook access levels from Public Domain to Subscription.
Access levels include Open Access, Locally Hosted (DRM), Perpetual Access (No Fees), Perpetual Access (Fees paid up front), Perpetual Access (Ongoing Fees), Limits on Circulation, and Subscription.
Subscription is the most restrictive and costly level, associated with short-term loans or rentals.
Public Domain is the least restrictive and free level.
visible_text: Perpetual Access Fees paid up front
